safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce from SAP 3.0 days to recommended 1.57 days

narrative: Material PL1__M4AA1B3D exhibits smooth, normally distributed daily demand (mean 1,621 units, CV 0.162) with no statistically significant trend over the observation period. The primary risk driver is lead time variability — a bimodal distribution with CV 0.751 reflecting a mix of short next-day deliveries and occasional 3–5 day replenishment cycles. The (r,Q) fixed reorder-point policy is selected because demand is continuous and smooth, enabling reliable trigger-based replenishment; the storage cap of 26,035 units constrains the order quantity below the unconstrained EOQ of 29,051, yielding a feasible order quantity of 23,486. Safety stock is increased from SAP's 1,972 to 2,549 units to close the service gap created by the high lead-time variance.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ 29051 exceeds available space (26035 - 2549 = 23486). Order quantity capped at 23486 units.
Lead time CV of 0.751 is high; bimodal distribution suggests two distinct delivery modes — recommend investigating supplier split or transport routing.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) — Fixed Reorder Point with Economic Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth (CV 0.162), continuous (100% non-zero), and normally distributed, making it well-suited to a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The deterministic reorder trigger combined with a fixed batch size minimises ordering frequency while maintaining the 95% service level. The MOQ of 986 is well below the EOQ, so it does not constrain the policy.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity cap of 26,035 units reduces order quantity from EOQ 29,051 to 23,486, increasing annual ordering frequency from ~14.0 to ~17.3 orders/year and raising annual ordering cost by ~$164. If the cap is not released, the service level is preserved but cost optimality is partially sacrificed.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (986) + safety stock (2,549) = 3,535 units, well within the 26,035-unit storage limit. No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
